---
title: "Install and run METIS"
---

## Try a notebook in Colab

Open a [tutorial](../package/quickstart.qmd), choose **Open in Colab** under
**Other Formats**, then **Runtime → Run all**. Its first cell uses uv to install
the matching METIS revision and tutorial dependencies. The examples run on a
CPU; no GPU or local installation is needed.

Colab creates temporary runtimes, so a new session needs setup again. Re-running
in an already prepared session skips installation. If Colab has already loaded
a library that setup must replace, follow the cell's restart instruction once.
See [Colab's explanation of runtime libraries](https://research.google.com/colaboratory/faq.html).

## Install locally

Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) and Git,
then create a project:

```bash
uv init my-surrogate --python 3.13
cd my-surrogate
```

On **Linux or Windows**, select CPU PyTorch:

```bash
uv add "torch>=2.10,<3" --index pytorch-cpu=https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
```

In the generated `pyproject.toml`, set `explicit = true` on the named index so
other dependencies use PyPI:

```toml
[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "pytorch-cpu"
url = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu"
explicit = true
```

On **Apple Silicon macOS**, use `uv add "torch>=2.10,<3"` instead. The current
PyTorch range does not support Intel Macs.

Add METIS with plotting support, then run the bundled example:

```bash
uv add "metis-surrogate[plots] @ git+https://github.com/OJWatson/metis.git"
uv run metis demo --steps 100 --output metis-demo
```

This saves a model, metrics and predictions in `metis-demo/`. uv keeps your
project's dependencies in `pyproject.toml`, resolved versions in `uv.lock`,
and environment in `.venv`. Keep the first two with your analysis. Run scripts
with `uv run python your_script.py`; no environment activation is necessary.

The distribution is **metis-surrogate**, imported as **metis**. It is not yet
on PyPI; the PyPI package named `metis` is unrelated. Python 3.11+ is supported.
Optional extras are `plots`, `pandas`, `wandb` and `docs`; include the ones you
need together in the dependency requirement.

## Run downloaded notebooks

Add the tutorial dependencies and JupyterLab to the same project:

```bash
uv add "metis-surrogate[docs] @ git+https://github.com/OJWatson/metis.git"
uv add --dev jupyterlab
uv run jupyter lab
```

Download **Jupyter** under a tutorial's **Other Formats**, save it in this project,
and open it in JupyterLab. Its saved outputs are already visible; use **Run all**
to regenerate them. In another notebook editor, select this project's `.venv`
Python kernel. Keep any other extras you use in the `uv add` requirement.

## Optional CUDA setup

For NVIDIA GPUs, select an index compatible with your driver using the
[uv PyTorch guide](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/integration/pytorch/).
For example, if CUDA 12.8 is appropriate:

```bash
uv add "torch>=2.10,<3" --index pytorch-cu128=https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128
```

Set `explicit = true` on the new `pytorch-cu128` index as above. This updates
Python dependencies, not your NVIDIA driver. Check the result and train:

```bash
uv run python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__, torch.cuda.is_available())"
uv run metis train model=mlp training.device=cuda
```

In Python, use `TrainingConfig(device="cuda")`.
